sentences.text:
Surajprasad @ Rajkumar vs The State Of Maharashtra on 8
October, 2025
Bench: Sanjay Karol, Prashant Kumar Mishra
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal Nos. 1367-1368 Of 2018
 Surajprasad @ Rajkumar Appellant(S
 Versus
 The State Of Maharashtra Respondent(S)
 Order
1.

The appellant stands convicted for having committed offence punishable under Section 376(2)(f)(i) of the Indian Penal Code 1860 read with Sections 4 and 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The crime was committed on 14th July 2013.

Both the Courts below,
in our considered view have minutely examined the materials placed on record, in returning the findings of fact, with regard to the appellants guilt.
2. As such, we are not inclined to interfere with the same.

We ourselves have perused the testimonies of the material witnesses, i.e., the victim; her mother; and the doctor and found nothing on record which would impeach their credit or render their testimonies to be unbelievable.
The witnesses cannot be said to be unreliable or the accused being close relative of the victim, was falsely implicated.
3. As such we proceed now to examine as to whether the quantum of sentence of imprisonment requires interference or not.

4. The Trial Court directed the appellant-convict to suffer imprisonment for a period of 10 years and pay a fine of Rs.1000/- in relation to offence punishable under Section 376(2)(f)(i) of the IPC and in default to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for three months; and in relation to Section 506 of the IPC he was to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for 1 year and to pay fine of Rs.500/-.

These sentences were Surajprasad @ Rajkumar vs The State Of Maharashtra on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12969871/
1 to run concurrently.

sentences.text: However, the Appellate Court enhanced the said sentence to that of life.

5. Having weighed the materials placed on record and the attending facts and circumstances, more so considering the current age of the appellant-accused, his medical condition, and also the fact that he has already served sentence of approximately 12 years, we reduce the sentence of life imprisonment to the sentence already undergone, which in fact, is in excess of what stood awarded by the Trial Court.
Accordingly, the appeals are allowed.
The appellant-convict be set at liberty forthwith if he is not required in any other case.
Pending applications(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

J. (SANJAY KAROL) J. (PRASHANT KUMAR MISHRA) New Delhi;

4. The Trial Court directed the appellant-convict to suffer imprisonment for a period of 10 years and pay a fine of Rs.1000/- in relation to offence punishable under Section 376(2)(f)(i) of the IPC and in default to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for three months; and in relation to Section 506 of the IPC he was to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for 1 year and to pay fine of Rs.500/-.
However, the Appellate Court enhanced the said sentence to that of life.
5. Having weighed the materials placed on record and the attending facts and circumstances, more so considering the current age of the appellant-accused, his medical condition, and also the fact that he has already served sentence of approximately 12 years, we reduce the sentence of life imprisonment to the sentence already undergone, which in fact, is in excess of what stood awarded by the Trial Court.
Accordingly, the appeals are allowed.
The appellant-convict be set at liberty forthwith if he is not required in any other case.
